editorial: The open-sourcing of the Mistral Large 4 model weights and the release of new language models like DeepSeek V4.1 Flash have caused significant activity in the developer ecosystem today. On the academic side, studies examining the impact of benchmark methods on difficulty levels are reopening the debate on model evaluation processes.

items.title: HKUDS/DeepTutor
items.summary: HKUDS/DeepTutor is an agent-native AI-based educational workspace that combines learning processes such as tutoring, problem-solving, exam creation, and research into a single system. Aiming to make personalized learning experiences continuous for users, this system offers visualization and expertise practices in an extensible structure.

snapshot.description: DeepTutor: Lifelong Personalized Tutoring. DeepTutor is an agent-native learning workspace that connects tutoring, problem solving, quiz generation, research, visualization, and mastery practice in one extensible system.

items.title: obra/superpowers
items.summary: obra/superpowers is a software development methodology and framework developed for AI coding agents. It enables agents to structure software development processes through composable skills and core instructions.

snapshot.description: An agentic skills framework & software development methodology that works. Superpowers is a complete software development methodology for your coding agents, built on top of a set of composable skills and some initial instructions that make sure your agent uses them.

items.title: pbakaus/impeccable
items.summary: Developed in Rust, impeccable offers a design vocabulary for coding agents. It aims to detect AI-generated erroneous content (AI slop) during the software development process and improve the quality of projects.

snapshot.description: The design vocabulary for your coding agent. Steer with polish and bolder, review with critique and audit, catch AI slop before it ships.

items.title: JetBrains/thinkrail
items.summary: ThinkRail, developed by JetBrains, is an agentic Integrated Development Environment (IDE) that adapts to the user's working style and improves its capabilities over time by learning project requirements. Prepared with the TypeScript language, this tool aims to personalize the developer experience by analyzing projects through living specifications.

snapshot.description: Vibe code with pi in a lightweight, real IDE that customises itself around the way you work — The Vibe You Need. ThinkRail is the agentic IDE that gets better every time you use it — learning your project through living specs today, and building its own capabilities tomorrow.

items.title: milind-soni/OpenMausBot
items.summary: OpenMausBot is an open-source Grok Bot alternative that allows you to create your own AI bot team within chat applications. The software comes with virtual machine support that the bots can utilize.

snapshot.description: Open-source Grok Bot alternative with a virtual machine that bots can use. The open-source Grok Bot alternative: your own team of AI bots, in a chat app.

items.title: nightly-labs/openbot
items.summary: nightly-labs/openbot is a desktop application that allows you to run AI models like Codex, Claude, and Grok in local workspaces. The software provides an environment that supports collaboration among AI-based teammates with features such as file sharing and browser control.

snapshot.description: A local-first desktop workspace for persistent AI teammates. Run Codex, Claude, and Grok with dedicated workspaces, task queues, file sharing, browser control, and agent-to-agent collaboration.

items.title: elayadesign/ai-design-skills
items.summary: elayadesign/ai-design-skills is a collection of design skills prepared for AI coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf) intended for systems that can read markdown rules. It offers standardized instructions that allow developers to get more efficient results from these tools.

snapshot.description: A growing collection of design skills for AI coding tools — Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf, and anything else that reads a markdown rules file.

items.title: thedotmack/claude-mem
items.summary: thedotmack/claude-mem is a tool that saves the history of AI agents between sessions, providing context for future interactions. Working with coding assistants like Claude Code and Copilot, this system compresses data with AI to transfer relevant information to subsequent sessions.

snapshot.description: Persistent Context Across Sessions for Every Agent – Captures everything your agent does during sessions, compresses it with AI, and injects relevant context back into future sessions. Works with Claude Code, OpenClaw, Codex, Gemini, Hermes, Copilot, OpenCode + More

items.title: CopilotKit/OpenBot
items.summary: CopilotKit/OpenBot enables the creation of open-source AI coworkers that can access tools such as browsers and files. This system supports any user interface agent (AG-UI agent) integration with a structure that plans every action before executing it and records it afterward.

snapshot.description: Open-source AI coworkers that each get a computer of their own: a browser, files and tools, with every action decided before it happens and recorded after. Bring any AG-UI agent.

items.title: Donchitos/Claude-Code-Game-Studios
items.summary: Claude-Code-Game-Studios is a project that aims to transform the Claude Code software development tool into a comprehensive game studio. It offers a coordination system that mimics a real studio hierarchy by using 49 AI agents and 72 workflow skills.

snapshot.description: Turn Claude Code into a full game dev studio — 49 AI agents, 72 workflow skills, and a complete coordination system mirroring real studio hierarchy.

items.title: Patrick Stewart has died
items.summary: According to news published by the New York Times, actor Patrick Stewart has passed away. The news of the artist's death received widespread coverage on social platforms.

snapshot.description: https://archive.ph/y4Egmhttps://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Stewart

items.title: We're releasing the weights of Mistral Large 4
items.summary: Mistral AI has released the weights of its large language model, Mistral Large 4, as open source. This move allows developers to run and customize the model on their own infrastructure.

items.title: Binance-hacker-1029 – $5.6B stolen from Binance
items.summary: It is alleged that assets worth 5.6 billion dollars were stolen from the Binance cryptocurrency exchange via a digital wallet named Binance-hacker-1029. These data, shared by the blockchain analysis platform Arkham Intelligence, allow for tracking the activity at the wallet address in question.

items.title: DoorDash to acquire Instacart
items.summary: Food delivery platform DoorDash has announced that it will acquire the grocery delivery service Instacart. With this merger, it is aimed for stores of all sizes to reach a wider customer base by accessing the technological infrastructure used by large online retailers.

snapshot.description: Together, DoorDash and Instacart would help stores of every size reach more customers with the kinds of innovative technology that the biggest online retailers and grocers build for themselves.

items.title: LLM Voice
items.summary: LLM Voice, written by Martin Fowler, addresses the artificiality in texts generated by large language models (LLMs) and the uncanny valley effect this situation creates. The article evaluates the characteristic stylistic issues present in AI-generated content despite its similarity to human language.

snapshot.description: The uncanny valley of LLMs' prose

items.title: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017
items.summary: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017, published on Hugging Face, is an AI model capable of processing visual and text-based data. Compared to the previous version, it aims to reduce processing time and costs while offering improvements in areas such as reasoning, coding, and visual analysis.

snapshot.description: image-text-to-text model. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 is a minor update to DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, delivering substantial improvements across reasoning, coding, agentic tasks, and visual benchmarks. Alongside these gains, the model reduces task execution time and output length, enabling users to complete tasks faster and at lower cost and advancing the performance–cost Pareto frontier across multiple agent harnesses.

items.title: Nanbeige/Nanbeige4.3-33B
items.summary: Nanbeige/Nanbeige4.3-33B, shared on Hugging Face, is presented as an AI model focused on text generation. Developers aim to create lightweight AI agents by targeting the distillation of capabilities into smaller models via a high-capacity teacher model.

snapshot.description: text-generation model. In Nanbeige4.3, we take a foundational step toward pushing the boundaries of lightweight agents. Our strategy centers on building a high-capacity teacher agent first, which will subsequently anchor the distillation of advanced agentic capabilities into smaller models.

items.title: LiquidAI/LFM3-1.7B
items.summary: LFM3-1.7B, developed by LiquidAI, is a text-generation model designed for local agents and specialized applications. Based on a new tri-hybrid architecture, this model aims to provide efficient performance with a low parameter count.

snapshot.description: text-generation model. LFM3-1.7B is a text model for local agents and specialized applications, based on our new tri-hybrid architecture.

items.title: RecursiveSI/flint
items.summary: Flint, developed by RecursiveSI, is a mixture-of-experts language model designed for coding-focused AI agents. With a total of 39.8 billion parameters, the model was developed to perform tasks such as examining codebases, debugging, adding features, and writing tests.

snapshot.description: text-generation model. Flint is Recursive’s mixture-of-experts language model for coding agents, with 39.8 billion total parameters and approximately 2.5 billion active per token. It is designed to investigate codebases, fix bugs, implement features, and write tests.

items.title: XHToken/Spark-X2.6-4B
items.summary: Spark-X2.6-4B, published on Hugging Face, is an AI model focused on text generation. Maintaining the same architecture as Spark-X2.5-4B, this version offers more advanced performance in areas such as coding, multilingualism, and reasoning thanks to improvements in the post-training process.

snapshot.description: text-generation model. Spark-X2.6-4B retains exactly the same architecture as Spark-X2.5-4B, achieving its capability gains through improved post-training. It delivers substantial improvements in coding, agent, long-context, multilingual, reasoning, etc. These advances enable more capable and practical on-device AI for developers and users tackling real-world tasks.

items.title: Intrinsic Distribution Matching
items.summary: Intrinsic Distribution Matching, shared by Hugging Face, aims to achieve high accuracy with a limited number of steps in text-to-image generation processes. Based on the distribution matching distillation method, this study examines the effects of an explicit moment constraint for the convergence of generated images to the reference distribution.

snapshot.description: One-step and few-step text-to-image generation must accurately render the details specified in the prompt despite limited opportunities for refinement. Distribution matching distillation (DMD) uses score differences to bring the generated distribution closer to a reference distribution. Following prior work, we estimate this difference with internal velocity branches, avoiding a separate fake-score network. items.title: Your Benchmark Is an Empirical Measure Over Difficulty
items.summary: The article shared by Hugging Face defines benchmark tests not just as collections of questions, but as empirical measurement tools based on difficulty levels. This perspective aims to make evaluation processes more systematic by identifying fundamental failure modes such as measurement misalignment and coverage gaps.

snapshot.description: A benchmark is not merely a collection of test questions; it naturally induces an empirical measure over difficulty. In this work, we develop this measure-based view of benchmark evaluation. This perspective allows us to identify and formalize two central failure modes: measure mismatch, where the benchmark difficulty distribution differs from the intended difficulty distribution, and coverage gaps, where uncovered regions along the difficulty axis prevent benchmarks from detecting meaningful lo

items.title: A Broader Look into MLLM's Retrieval Heads
items.summary: The article shared by Hugging Face examines the retrieval heads that provide multimodal large language models with the ability to find evidence in long inputs. The study questions the effect of this mechanism across different modes and how it can be used to improve models.

snapshot.description: Locating relevant evidence in long inputs is a core capability of Multimodal Large Language Models. Prior studies attribute this capability to retrieval heads, a sparse set of attention heads that transfer information from the context to the output. However, these analyses are confined to a limited set of modalities and the corresponding models. Moreover, how retrieval heads can be leveraged to enhance the model calls for further exploration. In this paper, we ask whether this mechanism expands

items.title: Co-Design Bench: Multimodal Collaborative Coding Evaluation for Agentic Models
items.summary: Co-Design Bench, shared by Hugging Face, is an evaluation tool that measures the ability of AI coding agents to translate real users' multimodal requests into application changes. Containing 273 tasks across two distinct areas—multimodal editing and repository editing—this benchmark was created using data obtained from real user sessions.

snapshot.description: Evaluating human-AI co-design requires testing whether coding agents can translate real users' multimodal requests into working application revisions. We introduce Co-Design Bench, a reference-free benchmark of 273 tasks curated from 37,463 deduplicated queries across 26,314 real user coding sessions. items.title: AskStream: When and What to Ask Proactively under Uncertainty in Streaming Video Understanding
items.summary: AskStream offers an interactive method that determines when and what an AI should ask in cases of uncertainty during streaming videos. It aims to transform multimodal large language models from passive responders into agents that proactively query for missing information.

snapshot.description: Recent advances in multimodal large language models have increased interest in interaction paradigms for video understanding. The evolution from offline to streaming and proactive interaction has gradually shifted models from passive responders toward more proactive agents that can decide when to answer. glossary.explanation: A system designed directly according to the operating principles of AI agents, shaped according to the needs of the agents.
A structure that offers a set of specific rules and tools used to facilitate software development processes.
Modular capabilities that can be combined and used in different ways according to need.
A standardized set of commands and terms that enable agents to understand each other during software development.
The entirety of low-quality, erroneous, or unnecessary content generated by artificial intelligence.
A comprehensive work environment that enables software developers to write, edit, and debug code.
Software whose source code is open for anyone to access, examine, and improve.
The knowledge base based on past interactions that AI needs to provide more consistent answers.
AI software capable of performing operations via a user interface, reading the screen, and executing actions such as clicking or typing.
Specific task definitions and capabilities required to complete a particular business process step-by-step.
Numerical values that store the information learned by an artificial intelligence model during training and determine the model's decision-making process.
Artificial intelligence models trained on vast amounts of data that can understand human language and generate text.
The feeling of unease that arises when content generated by artificial intelligence looks very similar to human work but does not appear completely natural.
The process of creating meaningful sentences and texts based on given prompts.
The process of transferring the knowledge of a large and complex artificial intelligence model to a smaller, faster-running model.
Fast and efficient artificial intelligence software capable of running with low processing power.
